channel.title: Newest Python PEPs
channel.description: Newest Python Enhancement Proposals (PEPs): Information on new language features and some meta-information like release procedure and schedules.

item.title: PEP 846: Docstrings for Type Aliases
item.description: This PEP proposes preserving a string literal immediately following a type statement as the resulting type alias object’s __doc__ attribute, exposing that documentation through ast, and displaying it through pydoc and help(). It follows the placement already supported by source-based documentation tools. The parser stores the docstring in a new optional doc field on ast.TypeAlias instead of creating a separate ast.Expr node for it. ast.get_docstring() retrieves alias docstrings from this field.
item.author: Bartosz Sławecki (bartosz@ilikepython.com)

item.title: PEP 845: Leading-Dot Value Patterns
item.description: This PEP enables the use of non-attribute names as value patterns in match statements. A name prefixed with a dot is looked up using the normal name resolution rules and compared to the match subject by equality in the same manner as existing value patterns, instead of being treated as a capture pattern. This makes it possible to match local variables and global variables defined in the same module without using a guard clause.
item.author: Thomas Kehrenberg (tmke8@posteo.net), (Marc)

item.title: PEP 847: Problem Details for the Simple Repository API
item.description: This PEP proposes standardizing the format of error responses returned by the simple repository API.
item.author: Luis Gonzalez (lgonzalez@sonatype.com), William Woodruff (william@yossarian.net), Zsolt Dollenstein (zsol.zsol@gmail.com)

item.title: PEP 844: ``public`` and ``private`` builtins
item.description: This PEP proposes adding two new builtin functions, public() and private(), which document the public interface of a module by keeping its __all__ synchronized with the names actually defined to be public in that module. Both are used as decorators (@public and @private) on class and function definitions, so that a name’s visibility is declared exactly once, at the point where the name is defined. public() additionally has a function call form for names that cannot be decorated, such as constants.
item.author: Barry Warsaw (barry@python.org)

item.title: PEP 843: Export Statement for DRY Re-exports
item.description: Large libraries separate their implementation layout (the tree of modules convenient for maintainers) from their public layout (the shallower, curated tree they present to users). Building that public layout today means choosing between two imperfect options.
item.author: Neil Girdhar (mistersheik@gmail.com)

item.title: PEP 842: Module Exports
item.description: This PEP proposes an export statement that modules can use to express intent about the visibility of variables from outside the module.
item.author: Peter Bierma (peter@python.org)

item.title: PEP 841: Adding Frozen Syntax to Optimize Immutable Types
item.description: This PEP proposes frozen display syntax: f{1, 2, 3} evaluates to a frozenset, and f{'a': 1} evaluates to a frozendict. Because immutability is guaranteed by the syntax itself rather than inferred from usage, the compiler can treat frozen displays as first-class citizens of its optimization pipeline: constant displays are folded into a single LOAD_CONST with an exact result type at compile time and cached in .pyc files.
item.author: Donghee Na (donghee.na@python.org), Nikita Sobolev (mail@sobolevn.me)

item.title: PEP 840: Name Resolution in Class Namespaces
item.description: There is a long-standing inconsistency in the way variable names are resolved in classes. Several alternatives to resolve this inconsistency are discussed.
item.author: Jeremy Hylton (jeremy@python.org), Guido van Rossum (guido@python.org)

item.title: PEP 839: PyFrozenSetWriter and PyFrozenDictWriter C API
item.description: Add two builder (“writer”) C APIs, PyFrozenSetWriter and PyFrozenDictWriter, following the design of PyBytesWriter (PEP 782). A writer collects items internally; *_Finish() produces the immutable object — a frozenset or a frozendict (PEP 814) — in a single pass, without ever exposing a mutable intermediate object.
item.author: Donghee Na (donghee.na@python.org)

item.title: PEP 838: Adding python-version to pyvenv.cfg
item.description: This PEP proposes adding a python-version field to pyvenv.cfg which records the Python interpreter used by a virtual environment. It records only the major and minor version to be resilient to patch version updates.
item.author: Konstantin Schütze (konstin@mailbox.org)
